analysis:
The PR changes only a test file, ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift. The hunk adds a test (head lines ~189-229) that checks the daemon state reports the enabled_models filter a committed model switch applied, and that a refused commit restores none. The supplied text is the BASE view of the file. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the new test body and any production-side changes to daemon state reporting are not visible.

I found no production code changes in this batch. That means no new attack surface, no changes to authorization, attestation, encryption, or the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), or the prefix cache (T-041). The test uses MockCoordinator and temporary directories under FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory. It writes only synthetic weights, with no real secrets or plaintext prompt data.

The existing tests in the file exercise relevant security-adjacent behavior: drain/lifecycle preemption, weight-hash recomputation after the files change, fail-closed admission after an unconfirmed commit, and rollback on rejection. The new test adds coverage in the same area and weakens none of it.

Remaining question for integration: the production change that makes the daemon state file report applied filters is outside this batch. If the state file's visibility or contents changed, it should be checked for information exposure. No evidence of that is supplied here.
